title: School Choice Is Not The Goal
author: Peter Greene
summary: Peter Greene takes apart a Heritage Foundation and Educational Freedom Institute piece claiming rural Texas teachers are out of step with rural families, showing that its evidence, a tally of 1,400 political contributions set against an election result, proves nothing. He then widens the argument: the movement behind such pieces is not really after choice but after replacing public schools with a system aligned to the Proper Values. He lists campaigns against LGBTQ charters, book bans and Florida's anti-woke push as further evidence. As with his other school-policy commentary, it is closest to Practice & Culture, since it concerns the politics and culture around public schooling rather than pedagogy.
points: The Texas teacher study leaps from donation tallies to a claim of ideological disconnect without checking who the donors are or how many teachers exist.
The pitch asks why rural families should be trapped in schools run by people with different values, framing choice as a culture-war tool.
Greene argues the real goal is a private system aligned to approved values, not choice itself.
Choice advocates have fought LGBTQ charters, book availability and diverse school options, which suggests they want schools reflecting their own values.
Such a system would not serve democratic, pluralistic public education.
quotes: They dug up 1,400 contributions by checking school district employees against zip codes with fewer than 500 people per square mile. Then they determined that 90.2% of those contributions were made in support of Democratic candidates. But hey-- Greg Abbott won re-election with 80.7% of the vote.

Here are some things they don't look at. How many of those school district employees are teachers? How many teachers are there total in those areas-- are the 1,400 contributions out of 100,000 employees?

In other words, the goal for these folks is not choice. It's to replace the current public school system with a private one that's aligned with the Proper Values, to wipe out any and all school systems that teach The Wrong Values.

We are seeing repeatedly that choice is not what some folks who nominally support choice actually want. Choicers have campaigned against LGBTQ charters. Patron choice saint Ron DeSantis is not in Florida fighting for every parents' right to have whatever school they want, but to Stop WOKE and CRT wherever it appears.
We don't really need choice, reads the subtext. We just need one system that teaches the things we want it to teach.
This is not a system that would serve anyone but a select few. It's not democratically owned and operated public education in a pluralistic society, and it's not actual school choice, either.
